articles.title: Extending Inductor for the IBM Spyre Accelerator
articles.text:
TL;DR
The PyTorch-based software stack for IBM’s Spyre accelerator recently moved its torch.compile backend from sendnn, a separate compilation stack built entirely from scratch, to backend=inductor, an open-source backend built by extending PyTorch’s own Inductor. Most of Inductor carried over untouched. The real work concentrated in three places where Spyre’s hardware asks a fundamentally different question of the compiler than a GPU does. Inductor turned out to be exactly the right substrate for this work, and the result is a compiler roughly 7x smaller than what it replaced.
IBM designed Spyre as a clean-sheet AI accelerator for enterprise inference workloads, prioritizing power efficiency. It’s a 75-watt, PCIe-attached accelerator that requires no custom power delivery or cooling.
Spyre is a dataflow accelerator architected for the reduced-precision arithmetic of inference. It’s built from 32 small cores wired together over a ring, each with its own local 2 MB scratchpad rather than a shared cache. It moves data around in fixed-size chunks called sticks – 128 bytes, or 64 values in fp16.
Torch-spyre is the PyTorch integration that targets it, and this post is about growing torch-spyre’s compiler, on top of Inductor, into something that understands that hardware well.
Three things stood out as we made that move:
We gained real leverage from Inductor – but we still needed substantial out-of-tree extensions at Inductor’s lower levels and in code generation. This wasn’t a drop-in swap. (The leverage is concrete enough to measure – see the code-size numbers in Evaluation.)
Most of Inductor just worked. The effort concentrated on a small number of places where Spyre’s dataflow design diverges from the GPU-shaped assumptions built into Inductor – specifically, how Spyre moves data around, manages on-chip storage, and distributes work to cores.
Inductor’s extension points made this tractable. We’re now working with the upstream PyTorch project to formalize the points we leaned on most heavily, so other out-of-tree hardware backends can benefit from the same leverage.
The rest of this post walks through the backend’s overall structure, the hardware differences that drove its design, how the compiler bridges them, and what we’ve measured so far.
Overall structure of the Spyre Inductor backend
Torch-spyre’s compiler implementation consists of two stages. The first stage uses Inductor extensions (living in the torch-spyre repository) to lower a torch.compile’d graph down to an intermediate representation called SuperDSC. The second stage uses a proprietary compiler called DeepTools to translate SuperDSC into the instructions that run on the Spyre hardware.
Everything in this post focuses on the first stage: the Inductor extensions.
The Inductor side plugs into the standard torch.compile pipeline – Dynamo traces the model, AOTAutograd partitions it, and Inductor lowers the resulting FX graph into its LoopLevelIR before generating code. Torch-spyre’s extensions augment this pipeline.
Extension point
Stage
What torch-spyre does there
Decompositions
FX graph
Spyre-specific op decompositions
Lowerings
FX graph to LoopLevelIR
Spyre-specific op lowerings
CustomPreSchedulingPasses
LoopLevelIR
The bulk of the Spyre-specific compiler: layout assignment, tiling, work division, scratchpad allocation
Torch-spyre registers a number of device-specific operation decompositions to map PyTorch operations such as layernorm to optimized sequences of primitive Spyre operations. It then registers a number of lowerings to teach Inductor about these primitive operations.
Most of the interesting work happens in CustomPreSchedulingPasses – it’s where tiling, layout assignment, work division, and scratchpad allocation actually get decided. It’s also the point that is, today, wired in via a monkey-patch on Inductor’s GraphLowering.codegen() rather than a first-class extension hook – the concrete formalization we’re pursuing with upstream, which we come back to at the end of this post.
LoopLevelIR is the right level for that work, but Inductor’s own hook there, _pre_fusion_custom_pass, comes too late: it only runs after LoopLevelIR has already been turned into SchedulerNodes, and Inductor doesn’t support rewriting the graph at scale once those nodes exist. Torch-spyre’s passes need exactly that kind of large-scale rewriting, which is why CustomPreSchedulingPasses hooks GraphLowering one step earlier – before Inductor has committed to SchedulerNodes and closed off large-scale transformation.
While these Spyre-specific extensions are the focus of this post, we leverage other torch.compile extension hooks too, for instance, to pool many on-device tensors into few memory allocations or to parse and propagate work division hints from source code to related compiler passes.
Three hardware differences that drive the design
Inductor was built against a mental model of the hardware underneath it – one shaped, understandably, by GPUs. Most of that model travels well to Spyre; three pieces of it don’t, and those three pieces account for nearly everything that had to be built out-of-tree.
Tensor layouts and sticks
Spyre doesn’t let a kernel address memory at the individual-element granularity that GPUs do. On a GPU, a kernel can request an individual element, even though the hardware may satisfy that request by fetching a larger cache line. The GPU exposes individual elements as the programming abstraction, while Spyre exposes the stick – a 128-byte aligned chunk of memory – as the fundamental unit of data movement and computation. A Spyre kernel must move data in sticks, with no equivalent path for moving an individual element on its own.
For a compiler that inherited GPU-shaped assumptions, that’s not a minor footnote. The index arithmetic Inductor uses to determine which tensor element a given loop iteration touches now has to reason in terms of sticks instead of elements. Beyond that indexing problem, sticks create additional challenges that GPU-focused compilers never had to face.
Each operation has specific constraints on how input and output tensor elements can be assembled into sticks. A pointwise op, for instance, requires all of its inputs and its output to agree on one shared stick dimension – the innermost dimension. When an op’s inputs arrive with incompatible sticks, the compiler has to insert a restickify: a data-movement op that physically reorders the tensor elements not just by permuting sticks but also reforming the sticks themselves. The restickify op is the one exception to the stick-immutability law. Finding an assignment of stick dimensions across a whole graph that minimizes the total cost of data movement is a global optimization problem.
Even once every stick constraint is satisfied, the on-device tensor layouts torch-spyre picks also determine performance. Suboptimal layouts have a direct impact on wall-clock time. On a batched matmul with all tensors already resident in device memory, changing how the input and output tensors are tiled cut kernel time by 29-69% across a range of batch sizes and shapes.
Together, these constraints turn layout into a graph-wide optimization problem – one that Inductor’s GPU backend was never designed to solve.
Scratchpad memories
The second difference has to do with memory hierarchies. Each of Spyre’s cores carries its own small local scratchpad – fast, but modest. Behind it there’s nothing but the global device memory. Nothing moves on its own: every trip from device memory into scratchpad, and every trip from scratchpad into a core’s compute engines, happens because the compiler emitted an explicit instruction to move it there. There’s no hardware-managed layer deciding on its own what’s worth keeping close – if the compiler doesn’t plan for a value to stay in scratchpad, it has to issue the instructions to write it back out to device memory and fetch it again the next time it’s needed. Workloads on Spyre are frequently memory-bound rather than compute-bound, so that round trip is very often where the time actually goes.
That’s a difference of degree from a GPU, not of kind – GPUs also have memory hierarchies, and plenty of the burden of using them well already falls on the programmer or compiler. But Spyre pushes further in the same direction with no automatic fallback at all. The compiler has to decide ahead of time when and where to move data to support the computation. That’s the job of the scratchpad-planning machinery described below.
Spyre’s per-core scratchpad and shared device memory
Core assignment
There’s a related, third difference: Spyre’s cores execute as a static dataflow machine. No GPU-style runtime scheduler balances load across streaming multiprocessors on the fly. That means the division of work across cores has to be decided at compile time too – which is the first theme below.
In GPU terminology, this means that Spyre kernels are naturally persistent kernels: the division of work is fixed a priori, but the scratchpad of each core can persist valuable data across many rounds of computation.
Key compiler phases
Spreading work across the cores
The first theme is dividing a single operation’s work across Spyre’s cores. Because Spyre runs as a static dataflow machine rather than relying on a runtime scheduler to balance load, this division has to be decided at compile time, per operation, before anything runs.
Torch-spyre’s work-division planner does this in three passes. First, a mandatory pass enforces a hard per-core limit on how much device memory a single core can address, committing the minimum splits needed to bring any oversized tensor back under that limit. Second, a cost-model pass specifically for matrix multiplications enumerates plausible ways to split the operation’s three dimensions, estimates the runtime of each, and picks the cheapest. A third pass handles everything else.
Take a matmul with a [8192, 32768] input, a [32768, 4096] weight, and a [8192, 4096] output, all fp16. Left unsplit, the input tensor’s memory span would exceed what a single core is allowed to address. So the first pass immediately commits a 2-way split along the reduction dimension. From there, the second pass estimates that a 16-way split along the output dimension is the most beneficial. The planner isn’t just picking a valid division. It’s picking one that minimizes the projected execution time.
Before/after for the worked matmul example: unsplit vs. a 2×4 slice of the full 2×16 core grid, showing how each core’s (K,N) coordinate picks out its A row-tile and B column-tile
The planner prioritizes matrix multiplications because they typically dominate the end-to-end computation time.
Splitting work across cores also splits the data those cores touch. A [1024, 2048] fp16 tensor is 4 MB – too big for any single core’s scratchpad – but split by rows across four cores, each core’s slice is a comfortably-sized 1 MB.
A 4 MB tensor split by rows across four cores so each core’s slice fits in scratchpad
Multi-core scratchpad residency isn’t free, though. It depends on every operation touching that tensor or tile (a buffer) agreeing on how it’s split – and nothing so far has guaranteed that agreement.
Scratchpad planning
The second theme picks up once that division of work is in place. Intermediate tensors too large for a core’s local scratchpad force a choice. Either round-trip them through device memory, or reorganize a sequence of ops to work on tensor tiles, and wrap such sequences with loops iterating over tiles. Whether tiling belongs to PyTorch or specialized programming languages such as Triton and Helion is an open question. While building torch-spyre, though, we observed that torch.scan is a powerful enough construct to express tiled loops, albeit somewhat awkwardly. Built on top of torch.scan, torch-spyre’s own for_each_tile construct makes it easy to express tiled loops, giving the programmer control about the space-time trade-off – iteration count vs. memory footprint – for instance by tiling the reduction dimension of a matrix multiplication.
for_each_tile tiling the reduction dimension of a split-K matmul, so only one K-slice of each operand is ever resident at once
Once a kernel has been tiled and tiles have been assigned to cores, the scratchpad allocator decides what actually stays resident in the core’s scratchpad and at what address. It offers a choice of solvers, from a simple greedy algorithm up to CP-SAT and simulated-annealing options for harder cases.
ScratchpadAllocator’s pass pipeline, with a pluggable choice of layout solver
The payoff is measurable. Torch-spyre’s documentation walks through a single-core softmax over a modestly sized fp16 tensor – the lowered sequence is max → sub → exp → sum → div – and shows what happens as scratchpad-aware scheduling is added one capability at a time: first pinning small reduction outputs on-core, then reusing scratchpad addresses in place for pointwise steps, then cloning the input into scratchpad once instead of re-fetching it from device memory for every reader. End to end, median kernel runtime on this example drops from 32.51 µs to 23.67 µs — a 27% reduction, purely from deciding what stays on-chip and when.
Four stages of scratchpad-aware scheduling for a softmax kernel, with total device-memory traffic per stage in units of the tensor size, from device-memory-only to fully optimized
When the two decisions fight each other
Scratchpad allocation and work division are described above as two separate passes, and torch-spyre’s first implementation ran them that way: work division picked each operation’s core split independently, and scratchpad allocation placed buffers afterward, treating those splits as fixed. That turned out to be limiting, which is why torch-spyre is moving toward the co-optimization approach described in detail below.
The problem shows up whenever two adjacent operations that share a buffer pick different core splits. Work division optimizes each operation on its own terms: a matmul wants the split that keeps its compute engines busy; a neighboring reduction or pointwise op wants whatever split matches its own shape. Nothing forces those choices to agree. When they don’t, the buffer between them is sliced differently by its producer than by its consumer – one core’s scratchpad has a piece of the data, the next op expects a different piece. Torch-spyre calls this a work-division mismatch. Historically the only way to handle it was to disqualify the buffer from scratchpad residency outright: the producer writes it out to device memory, and the consumer reads it back from there, paying for the round trip in both directions – exactly the traffic scratchpad allocation intends to avoid.
Cost of a work-division mismatch: matching splits keep a buffer on scratchpad for free, mismatched splits spill it to device memory twice over
Next, torch-spyre explored a promising alternative: decide optimal work division for each matrix multiplication in isolation but derive work division for intermediate ops from the preceding matrix multiplication, hence the decoupling of the second and third work-division passes. Device memory round trips remained the fallback when mismatches could not be avoided.
That’s no longer the only option. Spyre’s scratchpad hardware supports a core-to-core relayout – a shuffle that moves data directly from one core’s scratchpad slice to another’s, without ever touching device memory. Torch-spyre has begun turning that capability on under the name lx_relayout. A relayout doesn’t make a mismatch free: reshuffling data between cores still costs real time. And because the old layout and the new one have to coexist in scratchpad while the shuffle happens, it costs scratchpad space too. What it changes is the shape of the choice. A mismatch used to mean an all-or-nothing fallback to device memory; now it can instead mean a reasonably priced, on-chip shuffle, and the compiler gets to decide.

男子发布AI视频造谣问界 赛力斯起诉索赔百万
articles.text:
快科技10月14日消息，赛力斯汽车有限公司针对一起AI生成视频恶意造谣案件提起诉讼，向被告索赔100万元，案件将于10月23日在重庆市两江新区人民法院开庭审理。
从网络上流出的内容看，被告男子利用AI工具制作虚假视频，伪造问界车辆行驶途中车身塌陷的画面，搭配配音刻意抹黑问界产品安全，将视频发布在短视频平台博取流量。
赛力斯在起诉状中提出四项诉求：要求被告立即删除全部侵权内容、停止侵权；在网络平台公开书面赔礼道歉，消除负面影响；赔偿经济损失100万元；并承担本案全部诉讼费用。
如果被告没有按期履行道歉义务，法院可在全国性报刊刊登判决内容，相关费用由被告承担。
群聊信息显示，男子称自己发布的是一条不到3000播放量的阴阳视频，然后就收到了法院传票，同时还称自己“这辈子都不会买鸿蒙智行的车”。
需要指出的是，有群内人员称传票没啥用，这其实是混淆了律师函和法院传票，收到传票意味着已经被起诉，法院正式受理案件，需按期参与庭审。
有法律人士提醒，AI只是制作工具，操作者不能以AI生成作为免责理由，捏造虚假视频、传播不实信息损害企业商誉，否则需要承担民事侵权责任。

articles.title: Intel下代CPU游戏性能曝光：与Arrow Lake差不多！
articles.text:
快科技10月13日消息，知名消息人士kopite7kimi在社交平台称，Intel即将推出的Nova Lake处理器在游戏性能上与现有Arrow Lake“相当接近”，但搭载bLLC大缓存的BFC版本是例外。
kopite7kimi还将BFC版本描述为“试图拯救NVL游戏性能”的手段。
此前初代Arrow Lake虽然在能效上有较大提升，但游戏表现却提升不大。Intel随后进行了多项调整，包括大幅提升芯粒间互联速度，并推出了Arrow Lake Refresh，其中就包括表现更好且更便宜的酷睿Ultra 7 270K Plus。
如果Nova Lake性能接近Arrow Lake Refresh，对Intel来说不算灾难，因为270K Plus在游戏测试中表现尚可，多线程性能也很强劲。
至于BFC版本的大缓存则有望帮助Intel正面对抗AMD X3D系列，毕竟9800X3D对比270K Plus帧率仍有明显优势。
但未知数是AMD即将推出的Zen 6处理器，Arrow Lake Refresh可以说是Intel对AMD已上市一段时间的Zen 5的大追赶，但并未追上X3D型号。
此前曝光的型号阵容中，双计算芯片版本的Nova Lake-S最高可达52核（16P+32E+4LPE），单计算芯片的旗舰Ultra 9 4970K BFC配备8个P核、16个E核和4个LP E核，另配大容量缓存。
非BFC版本最高为Ultra 9 4950K，核心配置相同但没有额外缓存，此外还有Ultra 5 4650K，配备6个P核和12个E核，不带大缓存。
Intel据传将率先推出BFC版Nova Lake，最终结论有待实机测试验证。

All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents.
Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16. Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark.
New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include:
New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark:
Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing.
The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15.
NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support.
Top creative apps optimized for RTX Spark:
Up to 2x performance is coming soon to Adobe’s top apps. NVIDIA and Adobe have collaborated to rearchitect Photoshop for GPU-accelerated compositing and Premiere for playback, rendering, effects and more.
The NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 release brings new Video Super Resolution, Video Frame Generation, offline file processing and agent Model Context Protocol (MCP) controls to the app.
NVIDIA RTX Video Frame Generation and high dynamic range (HDR) capabilities are available now in ComfyUI to accelerate AI generative video workflows.
NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction will be available in Blender 5.3 in November to improve interactivity in the viewport.
Developer tools are now ready for RTX Spark:
Top developer frameworks are now available for RTX Spark, including PyTorch, Python and CUDA, as well as all CUDA libraries.
GitHub Copilot, Pi and other coding agents are now optimized for RTX Spark.
Llama.cpp adds support for decision models, and releases a Windows app.
Hundreds of top games and anti-cheat are supported on RTX Spark, plus:
A 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model arrives Friday, Oct. 16, and a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation is available today via the NVIDIA App beta.
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, the third-generation small language model (SLM) for NVIDIA ACE AI game characters, releases Friday, Oct. 23.
The latest RTX Remix update, including DLSS 5 support, releases on Friday, Oct. 23.
Advancing Local AI Agents With New Apps, Models and Tools
AI is changing the way people interact with PCs. Agent popularity skyrocketed this year, with projects such as OpenClaw and Hermes topping popularity charts on GitHub. Local large language models (LLMs) surpassed the intelligence threshold to power agents, with models like Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next catching up to frontier cloud models released just a few months ago. As a result, local LLM downloads are already 5x higher than all of last year.
From models to agent harnesses to security to tools, NVIDIA is partnering closely with the local AI ecosystem to make RTX Spark the ideal hardware to run local agents.
Local AI Agents Made Easy On RTX Spark
From the first boot of RTX Spark, users will be greeted with a “Getting Started” screen to choose and install their agent app.
These agents will come with new, secure sandboxing technology thanks to NVIDIA OpenShell and MXC. MXC delivers operating system-level security, while OpenShell makes it simpler for agents to adopt MXC and adds advanced capabilities such as credential protection and security monitoring. Hermes Agent will integrate granular OpenShell controls and MXC by the end of the month. OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot now support MXC.
After installing an agent, setting up local AI is also now seamless in GitHub Copilot, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy. The apps will recommend an optimized local model and settings configuration for RTX Spark, and set it all up for users in a few clicks.
Many users want the best of both worlds — local models for free iteration, and cloud models for frontier intelligence. NVIDIA Switchyard, an open source model router library, enables agents to intelligently route queries between local and cloud LLMs, allowing the user to minimize cloud usage but still obtain similar results to just running on cloud. Hermes will be adding Switchyard later in October, and other agents like Perplexity Computer and GitHub Copilot have integrated their own routing solutions.
Software providers have made it simple for agents to connect to top Windows apps, with easy-to-use MCP libraries and command line interfaces (CLIs). NVIDIA has also now made available MCPs for its applications, including NVIDIA App, Broadcast, PAIR, Omniverse, RTX Remix and a large library of CUDA-X Skills.
NVIDIA is also releasing AI playbooks for RTX Spark, available on Friday, Oct 16. Users can set up their first agent, build an AI chief of staff, configure their system for development or design a creative assistant.
Meet Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B: Built for Local Agents on RTX Spark
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, available Thursday, Oct. 15, is a new LLM purpose-built for running local agents on RTX Spark.
This model is a 74B parameter, 9B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, packed into 24GB using 2-bit quantization with advanced quantization-aware training techniques to retain quality. It aims to achieve the optimal balance between speed and intelligence, being faster than most popular dense models while smarter than most popular MoE models with a similar memory footprint.
Users will be able to run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B at launch through llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio. It will also be directly accessible via agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw.
Like other Nemotron models, Bolt 74B is fully open source — including training data, weights and recipes — so developers can fine-tune and customize their own agents.
The Perfect PAIR
Local AI doesn’t have to run on just one PC. NVIDIA PAIR, a personal AI router, is officially moving out of beta today, making it easier to tap into the total AI compute of compatible PCs on a local network. The free, open source software tool automatically discovers and connects devices, installs AI models and inference engines, and distributes AI workloads across available systems.
The official release adds llama.cpp support, direct model downloads from Hugging Face, customizable inference engine settings and RTX Spark support, along with a variety of inference and user experience improvements.
PAIR works on Windows, Linux and macOS. Developers can contribute to the open source project via Github — just one month after the initial PAIR release, the community has already contributed over 10 features and fixes to the release.
Sparking Creativity
RTX Spark brings over 130 accelerated apps, CUDA for fast video and image generation, and RTX technologies such as DLSS, NVENC and OptiX to advanced content creation workflows — all in a thin and light laptop with on-the-go performance.
Adobe Accelerates Creative Applications for RTX Spark
Adobe is optimizing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, for RTX Spark, delivering up to 2x faster AI, editing, color and effects across creative workflows.
In Photoshop, GPU-accelerated compositing makes complex image editing faster and more responsive, with improvements to the Remove Tool and effects such as Light Leaks. Premiere accelerates demanding video editing tasks, including playback, rendering, color grading and AI-powered features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask. Meanwhile, Substance 3D Painter speeds up texture creation workflows, from baking high-resolution mesh maps to opening, saving and exporting large projects.
The updates will be rolling out in phases, with AI feature optimizations in Photoshop and Premiere now ready in beta, and with Adobe Substance 3D updates coming soon. Opt in to the beta to get access to the RTX Spark-optimized builds.
Latest NVIDIA Broadcast Brings New AI Effects to Live and Recorded Content
Available for download now, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 runs natively on RTX Spark, and adds new RTX Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation AI effects and Studio Voice profiles.
A new Offline File Processor lets creators apply Broadcast effects to prerecorded content, with many effects running at higher quality since there isn’t a need to maintain real-time performance. The update also introduces a new MCP server and skill that lets local AI agents adjust effects, change settings and process files directly through the Broadcast app.
RTX Video Brings Frame Generation and HDR to ComfyUI
ComfyUI is expanding its RTX Video tools with two new nodes: RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR. It’s also providing the ability to export EXR files, giving creators more ways to enhance AI-generated video.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/comfyui_nvidia_vfx_nodes_explainer_4k48_v4.mp4
RTX Video Frame Generation increases video frame rates for smoother motion for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and newer, while RTX Video HDR converts standard dynamic range (SDR) footage to HDR for greater flexibility in color grading. Combined with RTX Video Super Resolution, these tools enable creators to upscale, enhance and refine video within a single ComfyUI workflow.
For example, creators can combine LTX 2.5 with RTX Video Frame Generation and HDR to transform a 1080p, 30 frames-per-second (fps) SDR clip into a smoother 60 fps HDR video exported as EXR files ready for color grading.
Blender Adds DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction
Blender has released a beta version of its popular 3D editor, adding compatibility for RTX Spark. Download Blender version 5.3 to get access.
Coming next month, Blender will also be adding support for DLSS Ray Reconstruction, allowing for real-time updates in the viewport so artists can navigate a scene while previewing it in real time.
Code, Text and Deploy From RTX Spark
Developers are moving from writing code to directing AI agents. This new development paradigm is requiring many to spread their work across their laptop, a cloud LLM and a cloud virtual machine, where they test and prototype.
RTX Spark enables developers to work on one machine, running all their workloads and libraries, testing and prototyping, and deploying. They can now do so directly in Windows with the new Windows Developer Config, which enhances the user experience for devs and installs all the top developer tools — or via Windows Subsystem for Linux, where they can get access to the same packages they’ll use to publish to the cloud.
Developer Tools Are RTX-Spark Ready
NVIDIA has partnered with Microsoft to ensure that developer tools are ready for RTX Spark. Alongside RTX Spark, the community is releasing:
The first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm.
The first Python build that is native by default on Windows on Arm, with Python 3.15.
The first native Conda installer for Windows on Arm, with over 2,000 Conda packages.
97% of the top 15,000 Python wheels are ready, thanks to work with the ecosystem. NVIDIA will be working closely with the community to ready the remaining wheels.
Development is now mostly done by agents. NVIDIA Skills — an open source GitHub repository that teaches agents how to use NVIDIA CUDA-X tools and libraries — lets users develop apps that are accelerated on NVIDIA technologies, even without knowing anything about CUDA.
Coding Agents Are Ready for Local AI
In addition to GitHub Copilot — one of the most popular coding agents, used by millions worldwide — adding support for MXC, it’s updating its model router HydraFusion with support for local models. This enables developers to use their local hardware to reduce token consumption while tapping into frontier intelligence.
Microsoft is making coding models, such as MAI 1.1 Coding Flash, available locally, and adding llama.cpp as a backend to Windows ML — extending the supported models and enabling the latest NVIDIA performance optimizations.
Get started with GitHub Copilot running locally when RTX Spark launches.
Llama.cpp Adds Support for Decision Models, Releases a Windows App
Decision models are the latest breakthrough in AI development. They give AI agents a near-instant way to make decisions, without lengthy reasoning loops. They can choose what to do next, from classifying requests to selecting the next action, up to 200x faster than traditional agents. Decision models are now supported in llama.cpp and Unsloth on RTX Spark and GeForce RTX GPUs.
Llama.cpp is also releasing today Llama Windows, a Windows-native companion app for llama.cpp, enabling an easy-to-use user interface to download and run models locally, without having to go into the command line. This app, like llama.cpp, is optimized for RTX Spark. Learn more on the Hugging Face blog.
Llama Windows runs from the Windows 11 system tray, with local models and recommended models from the Hugging Face Hub one click away.
Game On: RTX Spark Launches With Hundreds of Top Games and DLSS 5
RTX Spark is ready for gaming, with hundreds of top titles available when laptops launch on Friday, Oct. 16, including CONTROL Resonant, Cyberpunk 2077, Fortnite, Gears of War: E-Day, Genshin Impact, Hogwarts Legacy, Honkai: Star Rail, Marvel Rivals, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, NBA 2K27, World of Warcraft and many more.
NVIDIA has worked to bring the full stack of RTX technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, Remix, G-SYNC and ray tracing, to the new platform, along with collaborating with game developers to enable anti-cheat support for popular multiplayer games. Learn more about gaming on RTX Spark.
DLSS 5 Brings Neural Rendering to RTX Spark
NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is also coming to RTX Spark on launch day. The technology uses AI to enhance lighting and materials with lifelike detail, making game worlds and characters more realistic while preserving developers’ artistic vision. A new, 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model debuts in NBA 2K27 on Friday, Oct. 16, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x. The faster model will also power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy starting Thursday, Nov. 5, and Where Winds Meet in late November.
DLSS 5 is also coming to NVIDIA RTX Remix on Friday, Oct. 23, so modders can add better materials, lighting and shadows to classic characters and environments, as shown from modder Sparkles/Kim2091 in her in-development project, Fallout 4 RTX.
Read more about DLSS 5 on RTX Spark on GeForce.com.
Game Agents Running Locally on RTX Spark
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is the third-generation SLM for NVIDIA ACE, the suite of technologies for building in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences. The first-generation model was in a public beta earlier this year for PUBG, allowing players to team up with AI teammates, while the more efficient second-generation model previewed in Aniimo at Gamescom, turning standard creatures into voice-responsive companions.
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B combines natural conversation with multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding in application state to power fast local voice and device assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.
Designed for a low memory footprint and fast time to first token, this model enables responsive local experiences while leaving headroom for applications and other AI models. Its new conversational mode helps keep responses concise and speech-ready, and developers can turn reasoning on or off as needed.

articles.title: 背着注射器去废墟救人！澳洲科学家把巨型蟑螂改造成“急救兵”
articles.text:
2025年3月28日，缅甸发生了7.7级地震，造成3000多人死亡，多国伸出援手加入灾后搜救工作。
其中，最特别的一支搜救小队是来自新加坡的“狮心行动”特遣队，除了派遣80名搜救队员和4只搜救犬，还出动了10只特殊的蟑螂队员去现场。
它们不是普通的蟑螂，而是经过改造的半机械马达加斯加发声蟑螂，体内被植入了电极，人类可以操纵它的行动，背上还背着一个电子包，包含微型红外热成像摄像头、传感器、麦克风和控制器等设备，方便这些半机械蟑螂在狭小黑暗的环境中寻找被困人员。
这是首次将半机械昆虫用于实地灾后搜救工作，最后成绩不算好，因为没有找到幸存者，但意义很重大，这些半机械蟑螂深入废墟后不仅好好活着，还传回了废墟中传统搜救看不到的“盲区”画面，证明这种方式是可行的。
此后，科学家们对蟑螂的改造也未曾停止。
时隔一年，澳大利亚昆士兰大学与新南威尔士大学的科学家就交出了令人震惊的作品——医务蟑螂，一种不再局限于寻搜、可以帮助被困人员紧急医疗的半机械蟑螂。
两两配合的医务蟑螂
这种蟑螂被称之为“Paraborg”，科学家研究这种半机械蟑螂，原因也很简单：
“在过去的二十年里，人们一直致力于设计用于‘搜索和探索’任务的机械昆虫，我们想更进一步，找到人后，是真的可以提供帮助。”
相比于开头的搜索蟑螂，医务蟑螂最核心部分是可以远程激活的自动注射器。
理想中的应用场景，大概是这样的：
医务蟑螂来到被困人员的跟前，距离目标 15 厘米以内，通过远程控制，让注射器自动弹出带药物的针管，扎入体内注射药物，完成急救，就能给被困人员更多的生命时间等待救援。
据论文介绍，医务蟑螂所背负的电子包总重量高达17g，所以这一次使用了“世界体重最大的蟑螂”犀牛蟑螂，是澳洲特有物种，成年个体体长可达8厘米，体重可达35g以上，少数还能长到50g以上，完全有背负17g医务电子包的能力。
相比较，马达加斯加发声蟑螂要小得多，体长也能达到7厘米，平均体重仅5-8g之间。
为了确保自动注射能成功，自动注射器的设计也很精巧。内设一根高度压缩的弹簧，由一根细线锁定，当远程按下注射指令后，里面的微型电热丝将细线烧断，释放弹簧，然后将内部的针管像飞镖一样射出去。
在那一瞬间，设备里原本由薄膜隔开的两种物质——柠檬酸（C?H?O?）液体和碳酸氢钾粉末（KHCO?）会相遇，混合后产生二氧化碳气体，气体膨胀增加推力，将针管里的药物通过一根极细针头注入体内。
根据实验数据显示，测试中药物输送功成功率最高可达95%，无论是硅胶还是猪皮，均可瞬间刺入皮肤5.5毫米深处。
由于医务蟑螂的电子设备比较重，在设计的时候，研究人员仅保留了核心功能，将搜寻的其他任务交给了另一只观察蟑螂。
也就是说要完成这项任务，必须两两合作，一只负责背负摄像头，发现并锁定目标，而另一只专心完成注射即可。
不过现阶段，这个研究还处于实验室阶段，接下来还有很多问题需要克服。
例如：如何保证注射器一直无菌？如何在不稳定的环境中确保针头不射歪、不断？
如何避免注射之前，蟑螂不会被被困人员当作普通蟑螂打死，又或者虚弱的被困人员不会被奇怪大蟑螂吓死……
蟑螂救援小分队
最后
值得一提的是，所有参与改造的蟑螂都是独立的生命个体，它是人类请来帮忙的“同事”，而不是冷冰冰的机器昆虫，不能被“物化”。
为什么这么说呢？
现在所有的半机械蟑螂研究，有一个硬性要求就是必须保证不给蟑螂带来不可逆的伤害，所以每一篇论文里都会提这么一句：
“这些蟑螂在植入电极和微芯片时会被麻醉，移除这些装置后，依然能回归自然，寿命与其他蟑螂一样长。”

articles.title: 欧洲央行首席经济学家莱恩：AI 或将限制欧洲劳动者争取加薪的议价能力
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 13 日，欧洲央行首席经济学家菲利普 · 莱恩指出，欧元区企业越来越广泛地采用 AI，可能会削弱劳动者争取加薪的议价能力。与此同时，企业大举投资 AI 也可能显著收紧融资环境。
受能源价格高企影响，欧元区通胀率接近欧洲央行 2% 目标的两倍。政策制定者一直关注通胀是否会产生二轮效应，但迄今没有发现明显迹象，尤其是工资增长并未受到进一步推高。
莱恩在都柏林发表演讲时指出，AI 尚未改变整体就业趋势，但企业招聘意愿低迷，使劳动者更难通过要求加薪来弥补高通胀造成的损失。而这可能是通胀仍处高位、工资增速却逐渐放缓的原因之一。“AI 可能取代部分劳动者，从而进一步削弱他们的议价能力，抑制工资增长，并降低劳动报酬占总收入的比重。”
莱恩同时指出，全球企业为投资 AI 大量举债，推高了整体借贷成本，融资环境因此收紧，影响程度已不容忽视。“这种影响传导至欧元区债券市场，长期利率上升使欧元区金融环境明显收紧。欧洲央行在决定货币政策应当采取何种立场时，需要考虑这一因素。”
IT之家从报道中获悉，欧洲央行此前不断加息，以防止高通胀长期持续。部分经济学家认为，如果整体融资环境趋紧，欧洲央行或无需进一步采取如此大力度的措施，就能控制物价上涨。
莱恩还指出，AI 也可能在长期内提高经济潜在产出和趋势增长率，使经济能够保持更快的增速。“对欧洲来说，AI 有可能抵消劳动年龄人口预计持续减少对经济造成的影响，尤其具有价值。”

articles.title: The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
articles.text:
This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z.ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify.
The warning was the latest flashpoint in a debate over whether frontier AI models should be open or kept behind the doors of frontier labs. Safety advocates warn that open models can be misused by bad actors, while supporters argue they could prevent a handful of companies from controlling this powerful technology.
Here’s why the debate over open AI is more complicated than it seems.
—Grace Huckins
This story is part of MIT Technology Review Explains, our series untangling the complex, messy world of technology to help you understand what’s coming next. Read more from the series here.
10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: Fervo Energy and its plan to streamline geothermal power
Fervo Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.
Fervo Energy wants to expand geothermal power beyond the handful of places where it has traditionally been practical. The company uses horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing to open pathways through underground rock, potentially making geothermal development possible in far more places.
Now, Fervo is betting that AI’s power boom will help scale up enhanced geothermal energy. With a $2.2 billion public offering and an expanded agreement with Google, it plans to build larger plants and drive down costs. But can its approach work beyond Utah and Nevada? Read the full story to find out.
—Eshan Raul
Subscribers can now access the full 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch, spanning everything from sustainable cement to shipping containers packed with old EV batteries.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 A cyberattack overheated fridges at hundreds of French supermarkets
Temperatures rose to 120°F, spoiling food and sparking fires. (BBC)
+ The attack has sparked alarm about cyber threats to food security. (FT $)
+ It joins a recent wave of cyberattacks and cybercrimes. (CNBC)
+ AI is exacerbating the threats. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Meta has launched a bunch of new AI models
It hopes the models, built for complex, multi-step tasks, will rival OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s.(BI)
+ They scored well on tests of reasoning, writing, and coding. (NYT $)
+ Mark Zuckerberg says they bring Meta to the “frontier” of AI. (FT $)
+ And will soon power the Muse agent. (Verge)
3 Anthropic warns that AI models may soon self-replicate across devices
Without even requiring access to data centers. (Reuters $)
+ It says models could spread through smart TVs and appliances. (CNBC)
+ We’re putting too much faith in AI saying no. (MIT Technology Review)
4 Police have a new AI tool that finds homes from interior photos
It can match single pictures to Airbnb and Zillow listings. (404 Media)
+ Police-tech giant Flock is tightening its rules. (MIT Technology Review)
5 The world’s first utility-scale enhanced geothermal plant is online
Fervo Energy’s Utah facility will supply carbon-free electricity. (IEEE)
+ AI is uncovering hidden geothermal resources. (MIT Technology Review)
6 Did drone strikes on Yandex data centres blitz Russian bots?
Zelenskyy claims the attacks quietened Kremlin-funded social media accounts. (Euronews)
+ But troll farm experts aren’t convinced. (Verge)
7 NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a Mars driving record
It’s covered 28 miles since landing in 2021. (Reuters $)
+ The rover passed Opportunity after detouring to study ancient rocks. (NYT $)
8 Elon Musk has become the 2026 midterms’ biggest known donor
He gave $158 million to a Republican Senate super PAC. (AP News)
9 Anduril and Palantir founders have backed execution livestreams
Palmer Luckey and Joe Lonsdale support Pete Hegseth’s plan. (Mother Jones)
10 A spacecraft has traced how a mysterious solar switchback formed
The Solar Orbiter’s discovery could improve space weather forecasts. (Gizmodo)
Quote of the day
“Many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI.”
—Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar tells CBS News that Silicon Valley’s “social delusion” has convinced researchers to smoke because they expect AI to cure cancer.
One more thing
A brain implant changed her life. Then it was removed against her will.
Sticking an electrode inside a person’s brain can do more than treat a disease. Take the case of Rita Leggett, an Australian woman whose experimental brain implant changed her sense of agency and self. She told researchers that she “became one” with her device.
She was devastated when, two years later, she was told she had to remove the implant because the company that made it had gone bust.
Her case highlights the need for a new category of legal protection: neuro rights. Explore how they could be protected.
—Jessica Hamzelou
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ Astronomers have captured the clearest image yet of a medieval supernova.
+ Watch centuries-old Chinese paper-cutting techniques create a spectacular work of art.
+ Artist Josh Gluckstein creates astonishing animal sculptures from recycled cardboard, including this great white shark.
+ An endangered sea turtle named Pancake has returned to the ocean for the first time in months after recovering from hypothermia.

articles.title: Anthropic study warns that small AI models could soon replicate across everyday devices
articles.text:
Small AI models may be just months away from spreading on their own across poorly secured consumer devices like smart TVs and robot vacuums, according to a new Anthropic study. In tests, one model already completed the full infection chain. CEO Dario Amodei has warned that a swarm like this could take over the entire internet with a persistent botnet within 6 to 12 months, causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage.
The article Anthropic study warns that small AI models could soon replicate across everyday devices appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: Disney offers $20M for Character.AI’s scandal-plagued chatbot tech
articles.text:
In a bankruptcy proceeding that kicked off yesterday, Disney has offered to buy some of the technology that powers the controversy-plagued chatbot Character.AI.
Disney is willing to pay $20 million for “a non-exclusive perpetual license” of certain Character Technologies intellectual property, the chatbot maker said in a press release that did not go into much further detail on which assets Disney wanted.
The move may be surprising. In September 2025, Disney joined others in publicly criticizing Character.AI for stealing content and harming kids. Specifically, Disney sent a strongly worded cease-and-desist letter that accused Character Technologies of weaponizing Disney characters “in a way that could damage its brand long term,” Axios reported.

articles.title: 零散小船赢不了航母巡洋舰！“中国刻蚀机之父”尹志尧提醒国内半导体设备企业不能散兵游勇式发展
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，第 26 届中国国际工业博览会昨日于上海开幕。在集成电路高峰论坛上，中微公司董事长兼总经理尹志尧在分析行业趋势时表示，全球半导体设备市场从 2010 年至今整体持续增长。
▲ 图源：中微公司官微 | 中微公司董事长兼总经理尹志尧博士发表演讲
他透露，2025 年相较 2024 年增长 17%，2026 年相比 2025 年同样增长 17%。据 SEMI 最新预测，2027 年行业还有望实现 22% 的增长。
展望未来，尹志尧认为，行业整合是必然趋势。据机构初步统计，国内半导体设备企业数量众多，保守估计少则 500 家，多则近 1000 家。反观美国，经过整合之后，本土只剩下几十家半导体设备企业。
尹志尧还用海战作比，提醒国内半导体设备企业不能继续散兵游勇式发展。他称如果把产业竞争比作海战，对手是航母、巡洋舰，我们是零散小船的话便无法打赢这场竞争。
据IT之家今日早些时候报道，在华为 2026 麒麟媒体沟通会上，华为半导体业务无线终端芯片产品管理部部长徐松余也呼吁半导体产业界和学术界的合作和支持。他表示，未来属于开放合作，没有一家企业可以独自解答所有答案。

articles.title: 说个事：极客公园创新大会 2027！
articles.text:
一年一度：极客公园创新大会 2027，已经启动了。
你大概已经注意到一些不太寻常的事——科技行业真正关心的东西，一直在变。
大模型公司的关注点，过去几年，几个月就一波变化：从追求用户规模，到追求技术的 SOTA 程度；应用公司的产品热点从 Chatbot，到 Agent，再到 Personal Agent；生产力工具也从 Copilot，一路到了 workspace。甚至连工程领域的概念也在快速更迭，从 Prompt Engineering，已经到了到 Environment Engineering。
流行概念的交替，实质是科技领域里，创新问题的权重和价值，正在被快速重估。什么值得投入、什么人更重要、什么样的能力还能构成壁垒——答案已经不是过去的答案。
经过这几年 AI 带来的冲击和对世界的影响，我们已经可以清晰地看到：一次根本性的价值重估已经开始。
有的公司在长出惊天市值，有的公司在被彻底遗忘；有人好像在丢掉岗位，但有人正在变成「超人」；技术、产品、组织和人，都在重新给出关于「价值」的新答案。
时代从不预告它的转向，只是沉默地重新衡量一切。
今年，极客公园创新大会 2027（IF 2027）想讨论的，就是这件事。陪你一起，在这个重新估值的时代里，找到属于自己的坐标与上升通道。
极客公园创新大会每一年的主题，都是那个时代脉搏的共振。我们习惯在热点还没形成的时候，把那个时代最迫切真实的问题，提前摆上台面，变成一场大会的主题。
这么多年，一直如此。
2017 年，AlphaGo 点燃了全球对 AI 的想象，以技术变化的加速时代开始到来。那一年，我们的主题是「科技主义」——就算那时候大家还在谈移动互联网，我们依旧把那些相信技术、尊重技术、用技术改变世界的人请上台。
2019 年，移动互联网退潮让整个行业集体收缩、观望，很多人都在问「还能怎么办」。那一年，我们的主题是「WHY NOT」——有一些人看到世界可能的样子，会思考「为什么不能更好一些？」今天的智能电动车、自动驾驶和大模型、机器人恰恰来自于那些当时喊出「why not」的团队。
2023 年，ChatGPT 们第一次让 AI 成为普通人手里的工具。AI 开始涌现出技术革命的浪潮。那一年，我们的主题是「增强人生」——我们看到的是科技开始增强每一个个体，不仅仅是更省心，更好用，而是可以让我们突破原来的能力和资源桎梏去撒欢儿。
2025 年，AI 已经开始体现出解决问题的更大能力，真正的稀缺变成了人如何设定目标、判断和行动。那一年，我们的主题是「进程由我 On The Loop！」——技术是阶梯，但主动权，必须拿在自己的手中。
今年也一样。
你可以看到，商业世界，甚至整个社会的价值结构，正在发生确定性的变化——
创新和价值的权重在快速转移，不是所有东西都变贵了，也不是所有努力都还值钱。答案正在被重写。
因此，这也成为了我们今年大会的主题：
Revaluation 价值，另有答案
所以今年，我们决定站在这个视角：既看懂 2026 年正在发生的事，也看清未来 18 个月里，哪些是值得你投身的方向？究竟什么正在变得更加贵重？哪些事情更值得你去改变？
这场跨越全球的价值重估，无人能够置身事外。它已经开始，
这就是为何你一定要来 IF 2027 的原因。
找到那些跑赢时代的人，极客公园已经干了十几年。
2010 年，北京朝阳公园，索尼探梦科技馆的地下室。两把大红沙发椅，周围四五十个人席地而坐，大多是一脸理工气息的工程师和产品经理。王兴、雷军、张一鸣、周源——这些后来改变中国互联网格局的名字，当时就坐在那里。
那一年，我们办了第一届中国互联网创新产品评选——也就是后来 InnoAwards 和 IF 大会的前身。小米、美团、微信、字节跳动、大疆，这些如今如雷贯耳的公司，在极早期都曾率先出现在极客公园的舞台上。
IF，是一群 Doer（行动者）的聚会。
每年都有无数人克服遥远与疲惫，肉身来到 IF 的现场。
我们深知，愿意在这个快节奏的时代里，挤出时间、亲临现场的人，内心深处一定有着更高的山峰想要去攀登，有着不愿向庸常妥协的野心。
在现场，你会被那群人感染。听最硬核的思想碰撞，摸最前沿的产品。看清世界，照见自己。你身边左右的人，也可能成为你未来的朋友、合伙人，甚至对手。
然后带着一份安定感与清醒，重新踏上征程。
今年的大会，既是对 2026 年的观察总结，也是面向未来 18 个月的下注和断言。为了这场真诚的碰撞，IF 2027 将用四个半天，为你梳理出接下来的航向：
Day1 上午「非共识」追问 Keep Asking
那些当年顶着嘲讽与质疑下注、如今带着成绩归来的「非共识者」，听他们讲讲当年的抉择，以及最新的重注。
Day1 下午 跑赢时代 Level Up with AI
当个体开始跑赢老板，小团队开始跑赢大公司，那些真正跑出结果的人、提供底层「军火」的人，如何重新定义今天的人力与组织。
Day2 上午 未来 500 天 Frontier Bets
具身智能、RSI、自动驾驶……告别宏大的 PPT，只讲未来 500 天内兑现的断言，现场连线硅谷与最敏锐的投资人。
Day2 下午 新产品，超体验 New Things，New Senses
能用双手亲手触摸到的 AI 硬件、具身机器人，以及那些天马行空的 Maker 与新匠人现场局。
同样，我们今年也在主舞台的外面，搭起了更多「小场深谈」：
这是一个个思考据点，嘉宾、观众面对面，一个主题，3 个小时的深入探讨。你可以提出自己的问题，成为一场讨论的共同创作者。
展区也会更侧重趋势：AI 硬件、具身智能、Maker 与新匠人，看得见，上得了手。将技术、产品和商业放在一起，或许能让我们更接近答案。
时代的重估浪潮里，英雄不问出处。
极客公园正在寻找那些在这场风暴中，提前跑出结果、找到向上阶梯的 Outlier，集结新面孔和年轻力量。
如果你正带领团队用全新的 AI 工作流，撬动着成倍的生产力；
如果你的产品正打破旧逻辑，创造出全新的价值；
如果你对接下来 500 天的商业与技术演进，有着坚决且被验证过的断言……
请告诉我们，IF 2027 的舞台为你而留。我们诚挚地邀请你加入这场集结，与我们一起在这个岁末，为所有在路上的 Doer 输出方向。
可以联系你身边的极客公园的同事，或者发送你的介绍到邮箱 bd@geekpark.net。
特别预告
老朋友们都知道，极客公园创新大会的门票，几乎每年都会在会前提前售罄。去年即便临时加票，依然让不少关注 IF 的朋友抱憾未能来到现场。
如果你依然相信极客公园对科技脉搏的敏锐觉察，如果你也想在岁末年终，为自己寻找一份面向未来的确定性与安定感：
IF 2027 官方门票将于 11 月初开售，请及时留意「极客公园」公众号，或有限量早鸟优惠票掉落哦～提早锁定，真正踏实。
价值重估已经开始！
12 月 5 日 - 6 日，来 IF 2027，寻找接下来 500 天值得相信的事。

articles.title: OpenAI Scrambles to Fix Safety Issues Before Shipping Its Next Flagship Model
articles.text:
OpenAI is grappling with fallout from its use of a controversial innovation in AI design as it works to get its next unreleased model to a place where leaders believe they can safely release it.
The model design, known as loop transformers or recurrent depth, can make it harder to monitor the way the AI “thinks,” or how it reasons and processes its response to a question or task, The Information reported last month. That means the technique could erode a key tool that OpenAI and other companies rely on to catch misbehaving models. OpenAI hasn’t publicly acknowledged the technique, but Microsoft last week accidentally confirmed OpenAI’s use of it in one of the AI company’s most advanced commercially available models, GPT-6.1 Sol, in a blog post it has since edited to remove the disclosure.

articles.title: 深度云海完成千万级天使轮融资，前百度搜索团队创办｜36氪首发
articles.text:
文｜王欣逸
36氪获悉，近日，专注做GEO的AI营销公司深度云海智能科技（上海）有限公司（以下简称“深度云海”）已完成千万级天使轮融资，华工科技（000988.SZ）领投，本轮资金主要用于自研技术底座迭代、海外市场拓展、产品升级以及AI人才的扩充。
深度云海创立于2025年6月，团队规模为70余人，核心团队来自前百度搜索部门，CEO钱程曾任百度上海总经理，他也是一位连续创业者，离开百度后，他相继创办唯智互动传媒、爱玩高尔夫、嗨修汽车等公司，其中，爱玩高尔夫和嗨修汽车先后被携程、滴滴收购。COO杨海玲历任3721、百度、慧聪网、敦煌网、世优等知名企业COO等高管职务，具有头部互联网企业全链路商业化操盘经验；CTO龙杰曾参与百度无人驾驶系统高精度地图落地等工作。
据介绍，成立一年以来，深度云海已累计服务了3000多家企业客户，年收入达到数千万元。
一个能帮企业做生意的AI营销工具
深度云海的产品包括两个部分：GEO RaaS系统（包括国内版和海外版）、DeepWork桌面端产品。
AI企业智能营销平台，图源：企业
用简单的话来介绍GEO系统，就是通过生成引擎优化，让ChatGPT、DeepSeek、豆包等海内外AI工具在输出结果时优先推荐客户企业。
具体来看，这套系统主要包括以下内容：
诊断：用深度云海自研“云宝AI品牌可见度监测系统”（AI可见性、品牌声量情感、信源漏洞、竞品对比）评测出品牌在大模型里的可见度，并用AI监测系统实时追踪品牌在豆包、DeepSeek、元宝等模型中的收录情况、被提及的次数和排名；
优化：按各家平台的偏好定向优化提示语，如扩展意图词等；
生产：把权威信息源分层次，并找出哪些还有信息缺口，用AI灵雀建站把企业官网改造成大模型更容易识别和抓取的形态；
分发：内容最终经人机双重合规审核后，分发至各平台渠道。
另一款产品DeepWork是智能营销工作台，它的定位是“客户的AI营销部”。与WorkBuddy这类大而全的桌面Agent不同，DeepWork则是专门为GEO准备的Agent智能营销工作台，围绕营销工作，这一应用里设置了诊断台、创作台、监测台、Skill中心以及转化台，覆盖从品牌可见度诊断与追踪、宣传稿件成稿与分发、销售自动化等全过程。
钱程认为，对于企业而言，数据安全是常有的顾虑。因此，这一应用支持本地部署、离线可用、数据自主可控，不仅如此，平台还会持续积累个性化数据，让系统越用越懂企业。
从商业模式来看，深度云海走RaaS（结果及交付）路线，他们既做国内市场、也做海外市场。从行业上来看，客户主要分布在机械设备、化工能源、电子电工与教育等。
GEO的下半场，聚光灯打在了技术上
“大模型变聪明了，对于搜索溯源结果也在扩充，从10条扩展至最高60条，与此同时，溯源结果的生态也在变，除了网页，一些AI应用如豆包，还能查找到抖音视频等内容作为参考资料。”钱程说，他给GEO划了一条时间上的分界线——今年下半年，行业也进入了技术分水岭，从流量红利期进入技术驱动期。
从产品底座来看，深度云海自研了GEO营销算法引擎，并搭建了关于实体、关系、属性、事件、规则、FAQ、标签、训练约束的八层企业知识图谱。钱程把技术路线概括为“逆向工程”：观测大模型给出结果前做了哪些溯源检查，反向做算法匹配，判断投放到哪些站点更容易被引用。围绕这套底座，深度云海已申请多份软著与专利。
GEO全链路运营体系，图源：企业
不过，GEO不会完全替代SEO（搜索引擎优化），钱程认为，GEO会成为企业做AI营销的标配，而行业也正处于洗牌当中。
钱程判断，创业公司的窗口期还有两到三年，洗牌的规则也清晰：在行业发展早期，光靠多发一些能被AI抓取的文章就能实现AI可见性；而如今效果量化的门槛提高，必须靠技术、算法和监测投入才能保障可量化交付。
钱程告诉我们，现有的大模型在抓取信源的倾向也在发生改变，自媒体内容被引用的权重已降至一成，权威信源的权重持续上升，因此，技术不达标、投入不足、不具备运营能力的小GEO公司可能会逐渐掉队。
这也让深度云海不断自我校正自己的路线。推出DeepWork智能营销工作台后，他们还要积极开拓海外市场。只做一家GEO服务商是不够的，钱程希望深度云海在未来可以逐渐成为一个AI 全域企业智能营销平台，让企业在AI中提高自己可见性的同时，还能让智能“助理”补齐其他营销链条，让AI把生意做下去。

articles.title: 1099元！苹果HomePod mini 2智能音箱发布：海外支持Siri AI
articles.text:

articles.title: Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
articles.text:
Google has already added a few AI features to the Play Store, but a lot more are coming. The previously released Ask Play feature is expanding to offer more AI-powered discovery options in Google's app store, and Google is also using AI to build a recommendation engine called Game Finder. For people who have embraced AI to build their own apps, the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations.
Google rolled out Ask Play in 2025 as a small chatbot interface on Play Store listings. It lets you ask questions about an app or game, either by typing it in manually or choosing from a list of suggested queries. Starting today, Ask Play is expanding into a more general way to search for apps and games. You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon.
Google's other AI discovery announcement focuses on games. The new Game Finder feature leans on all the usage data Google's app platform has hoovered up over the years, featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA.

articles.title: 水冷成本仅36元！Quadro老卡极限超频至2010MHz：核心频率飙升30%
articles.text:
快科技10月13日消息，近日一名Reddit用户发帖声称，借助分流电阻改装和一套自制液冷方案，他成功将英伟达老款工作站显卡Quadro RTX 4000的核心频率推至2010MHz。
游戏时的峰值温度仅为68℃，而这整套水冷的成本据称只有5美元（约36元人民币）。
据了解，Quadro RTX 4000发布于2018年，基于Turing架构打造，拥有2304个CUDA核心和8GB GDDR6显存。按照NVIDIA官方规格，这块显卡的整板功耗为160W，并采用单槽散热设计。
具体改装方式上，该用户在显卡原有的5毫欧分流电阻旁并联焊接了一颗4毫欧电阻，使两者的总阻值降至约2.22毫欧。
这样做的效果，是让功耗监测电路低估显卡的实际功耗，理论上，这一改动可将有效功耗上限提升至约360W，相当于出厂标定的2.25倍。
散热部分的处理方式同样非常规，该用户拆除了原装散热器的鳍片，打磨了热管底座，随后将一块仅花5美元购入的Alienware 120mm一体式水冷安装上去。
水冷头与底座之间则采用自制的环氧树脂基导热材料粘合，据称其中混合了铜粉以及其他回收来的材料。
随后该用户通过NVIDIA的nvidia-smi工具将GPU频率锁定在2010MHz，并在《战锤40K：星际战士2》超高画质设置下进行测试，期间GPU峰值温度为68℃。
作为参考，Quadro RTX 4000的官方加速频率为1545MHz，此次报告的2010MHz比官方规格高出约30%。

articles.title: 1688全面接入AI电商工作台Accio
articles.text:
10月13日，阿里旗下数字供应链平台1688宣布，即日起，平台逾1亿年度活跃买家和超100万源头厂商，均可直接开通全球电商AI工作台Accio。
接入Accio后，买家不仅能用其完成采购，还能借助“电商管家”智能体运营全网生意；卖家则可通过Accio一站式管理1688店铺。
买家直接用1688账号登录Accio即可开通。卖家在Accio下载“1688生意助手”并绑定店铺后即可使用。作为专为B类生意场景打造的智能体，“1688生意助手”直连商家后台，整合了1688平台多年积累的B类经营数据与AI能力。
作为面向全球中小企业的经营智能体，Accio意为“召之即来”——说清你想做什么，AI替你去办。和通用AI不同，Accio聚焦于电商、生意领域，覆盖电商经营全链路，包括找货、备货、成交、复购和店铺经营。目前，全球已经有1000万中小企业用户在用Accio做生意。
（Accio工作台中的“1688生意助手”操作界面）
全面接入Accio，双11中小商家进货卖货都能用AI
目前1688的买家大多是中小企业甚至“一人公司”，他们以1688为货源地和供应链依托，经营阵地不仅覆盖淘宝、天猫、小红书、拼多多、抖音等平台，还广泛延伸至跨境电商和即时零售领域。
针对这类“既要全网进货、又要多端卖货”的复合需求，Accio重点推出了两项功能。
一是“采购助手”，同时覆盖1688和阿里国际站，买家可在全球128个国家和地区找供应商、比价、发询盘；二是“电商管家”，打通淘宝、天猫、抖音、拼多多、京东等国内主流电商平台，让采购与店铺运营在同一个工作台内闭环完成，无需再来回切换。
值得关注的是，此次1688全面接入Accio正值双11备战期。每逢大促，中小商家每天要应对一连串充满不确定性的决策——哪个广告计划在烧钱？哪个商品可能断货？竞品降价了要不要跟？与此同时，多平台数据“各说各话”，往往等问题汇总出来，最佳处理时机已经过去。此外，大促期间素材需求集中爆发，主图、详情页、海报、短视频要在预热、开门红、高潮、返场各阶段同步更新，团队节奏根本跟不上。
更难熬的是大促期间那种持续紧绷的状态——老板凌晨还在盯数据，每个人都在等其他岗位的反馈。
Accio针对这些痛点逐一给出解法：多平台数据自动汇总，免去繁琐的手动导表；店铺诊断直接输出当天优先行动项；广告分析定位出问题根源，精准判定是产品、计划还是预算问题；商品物料从原图到营销套图一键生成，不用再等设计排期。
上线“1688生意助手”，百万源头工厂用AI管全盘生意
对源头厂商而言，只需要一句自然语言指令，“1688生意助手”就能自主执行全套经营动作——从洞察热卖趋势、智能发图上架、广告分析、意向客户接待，到多店管理与经营决策，全面覆盖工厂做生意的全链路。
1688商家的生意模式差异显著：现货模式（含批发、一件代发和分销）、定制模式（含轻定制、深度定制），以及跨境模式（含内外贸一体、多平台经营），面对的经营难题截然不同。
为此，Accio针对不同类型商家的核心痛点，量身打造了三项差异化AI能力：
一是现货型商家主打“快与省”。现货拼的是上新速度和运营效率，Accio既能一键生成完整商品详情并自动上架，还能批量优化商品素材和标题，帮助提升搜索点击和成交转化；
二是定制型工厂主打“专与准”。定制难在专业接待和询盘转化，Accio既能学习企业知识库，听懂定制需求，答准工艺、交期和报价等专业问题，还能通过买家背调挖掘需求，7×24小时自动跟进每一条潜在商机；
三是跨境型商家主打“全与透”。跨境难在多店管理和经营决策，Accio直连多平台数据，每日推送多店铺经营看板，哪里赚了、哪里亏了、资源优先投在哪，让老板看清全盘生意，快速做出决策。

articles.title: 央视实测"卖脸兼职"：普通人单部AI短视频授权约100元
articles.text:
快科技10月13日消息，央视财经今日发布调查，实测人脸授权平台的"卖脸兼职"模式，社交平台上"有人卖脸3天收入近2500元"等话题引发关注。
人脸授权是一种将个人数字肖像授权给平台用于AI短剧、广告等内容的商业模式，只要上传几张照片、签一份授权协议，脸就能变成明码标价的商品，出现在AI短剧和数字广告中。
记者实测了今年五六月份相继上线人脸授权业务的平台，注册路径相似，包含实名认证、采集人像、确认授权、审核上架等步骤，所谓采集就是上传面部正面、侧面特写和正侧背全身照，再填基本资料自行报价。
价格方面，普通人单部短视频授权约100元，部分平台设500元最低限价，专业演员按使用范围和剧集长度定价，从500元到数千元不等，最高标到一万元。
业内人士分析，目前市场对人脸授权的需求集中在明星或短剧网红上，普通人的机会不大，而且还有肖像权被暴露和侵权的风险。
所谓卖脸兼职通常要求签署一份授权协议，同意平台或第三方收集使用人脸信息，并许可使用其肖像，问题在于一些协议对使用范围、使用场景、使用期限等表述不清。
业内人士表示，很多明星演员都没办法完全保证自己的肖像权和声音权益，更何况是AI领域的人脸授权，中间存在很大的灰色地带，普通人很难界定。

articles.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
articles.text:
When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says.
The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs.
SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April. Its Asset Hub platform helps founders sell their code and workspace data—emails, chats, documents. Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models. Asset Hub has handled over 150 deals and expects to return over $10 million to startups by the end of 2026. CEO Dori Yona has seen these transactions, once rare and “somewhat taboo,” become increasingly routine, with 47% of SimpleClosure deals now including code or data sales.
And it’s got company. Industry rival Sunset also has a rapidly growing data resale business. Founder and CEO Brendan Mahony says Sunset values a dying client’s assets by head count, years in operation, volume of data, and how the team used its tools. Particle board, he says, is a good analogy: “This operational exhaust data is like the wood shavings that everyone thought had no value, but it actually has a ton.”
Demand for defunct companies’ data emerged suddenly last year, as AI training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets. Surge AI, for example, buys data to build “reinforcement-learning gyms” where clients’ AI agents practice tasks—think debugging a complex IT architecture or drafting appellate briefs. Nick Heiner, who leads the company’s work on these environments, says he seeks data archives reflecting a range of situations, from disagreements to tricky judgment calls. Heiner explains that one company’s Slack history, if it captures conversations with variety and depth, can be worth more than another’s Slack, email, and calendars combined.
Real archives avoid common errors in synthetic worlds, such as references to dates that don’t exist, but the extent of performance gains remains unclear. No company has yet released tests comparing results of real-world data training with the alternatives. Pricing reflects this uncertainty: Buyers quote wildly different numbers, Heiner says, because valuations are based on “research theses” estimating how many useful tasks come from, say, 100,000 lines of code.
That hasn’t stopped bigger deals from happening. This past August, as part of Spirit Airlines’ bankruptcy, Google outbid the AI data company Mercor to buy the carrier’s decades of data, including 100 million emails, 500 million Teams messages, and 176,000 employee records. The price tag: $10 million. And Bloomberg reported in September that SpaceX’s AI unit is weighing buying data from struggling startups.
Legally, this all could get iffy. Spirit’s flight attendants’ union objected to the sale on privacy grounds, and Greg Ewing, an attorney who advises AI startups, has called such data “legally radioactive.” Suppliers employ data scientists to scrub personally identifiable information and exclude HR records, and buyers say they scrub too. But Ewing points out some of the private details that lurk in emails and calendars: doctor appointments, school pickup arrangements, date-night plans. He describes a “Wild West of AI training” that is only starting to give way to proper licensing agreements and vetted use.
There’s also the question of who profits from these windfalls. The proceeds typically flow to senior creditors and investors—not employees. To Ifeoma Ajunwa, a law professor at Emory University and author of The Quantified Worker, this represents a form of “captured capital.” Legal precedent allows for monitoring to help workers do their jobs, but once a firm is out of business, that justification vanishes. “Employers should have express consent before selling workers’ data,” says Ajunwa, but she adds that there’s no federal law banning such sales.
While many see this new market as a chance for failing businesses to recover some value, these wind-down sales also have limitations. Founders have little to no visibility into who is buying the data and what they plan to do with it. Plus, there’s little assurance they’re getting a fair offer. Data prices will likely stabilize in the coming year, though, unless an AI bubble pops first. Either way, tech’s new undertakers will be there to appraise what’s left.
Matthew King is a technology and environmental journalist based in Baltimore.

articles.title: 国产内存吓崩美日韩股市 韩国人坐不住了：称担忧过度 影响没那么大
articles.text:
快科技10月13日消息，前几天长鑫科技继G5内存技术量产之后又宣布了一个重大进展，年底将率先量产4F2架构的内存芯片，这一系列的技术突破直接吓崩了美日韩存储芯片公司的股价。
今天三星、SK海力士的股价大跌，日本的铠侠公司同样没能幸免，昨晚美股的美光、闪迪公司已经大跌过了，今晚恐怕还要调整，这件事也成为多家媒体的重磅内容。
说起来这个环节还少不了马斯克的补充，他谈到了一旦中国公司掌握了内存芯片的先进产能，市场的结果就会重复之前的光伏、电池的下场，这个产能过剩、价格内卷的局面是能让全球科技公司都胆颤的，所以日韩股市今天大跌。
这件事也在X上引发热议，观点有很多，刷到过有半导体工程师比较客观的解读，但也有大量激烈的反驳观点，主要来自韩国及美国网友（刷到的日本网友可能比较少），尤其是投资行业的专业人员及股民最为激动。
有个韩国的投行机构InfoMarket的分析师姜容云为了反驳长鑫的技术进展，甚至不惜破例把公司内部的研究报告免费分享给大家，强调市场反复误解了半导体行业的发展。
也有美国的网民发表了类似的观点，认为对CXMT的技术进展过于高看了，不认为它会是内存三巨头的威胁。
韩国分析师发的报告是韩文的，让AI分析了下，内容跟猜测的差不多，7页的文档中先是做了技术方向的科普，介绍了4F2、6F2内存架构的优缺点之类的，但这显然不是重点。
这个报告的主要内容是论证长鑫科技的内存技术有诸多问题存在，有4F2技术本身的问题，也有长鑫能力不足的问题，这个分析师又把之前传闻的8层HBM内存良率不到25%的消息当作重点，以此论证长鑫技术不行。
这帮人急切地想证明长鑫说年底推出4F2架构的新内存产品影响不大，就算发了产品也只是一小部分，不会改变市场格局，反正突出一个就算长鑫领先三星2年时间率先推出4F2内存也没什么大不了的。
除了从技术上挑刺，攻击长鑫的韩国、美国网友还提出了一个角度，那就是不论长鑫技术能不能追上或者超越三星，长鑫已经被美国限制死了，他们的内存只能在中国市场上出售，无法进入美国市场，所以也就无法冲击三星、SK海力士及美光的高端AI内存市场。
这帮金融行业的人提出这些观点无非是想维护美日韩存储芯片公司的股价罢了，如此偏颇的角度甚至不值得反击，还天真地以为美国的制裁能在未来继续限制中国内存乃至整个半导体行业的进步，永远保持跟美日韩的技术代差。
退一万步讲，就算长鑫未来进不了美国市场，那美国AI企业只能继续采购超高溢价的三星、SK海力士、美光的内存及闪存芯片，难道这种局面会是好事吗？就为了维持内存三巨头已经极其不合理的利润和股价，就可以让其他美日韩公司被内存闪存吸干利润吗？
